name: Photo angle maxxing
lead: Photo angle maxxing is the practice of finding the camera angle, subject distance, lens and head tilt that make a person look best in photographs. It sits in looksmaxxing communities alongside photography and lighting discussion.

Photography references explain that perspective distortion depends largely on camera distance: close shots with wide-angle lenses enlarge features nearest the lens such as the nose, while longer lenses used from farther away flatten them.[1] Portrait guides commonly cite roughly 75-135 mm (35 mm equivalent) as flattering for head shots.[2]
No studies were found that test whether choosing angles changes how attractive a person is rated, although research on perspective itself is described in photography references.
infobox: Camera angle, distance, focal length, head tilt, lighting

paras: Perspective distortion is the warping of subject and surroundings relative to a normal focal length, caused by differences in apparent scale between near and far features.[1] A face filling the frame through a wide-angle lens makes the nose look larger relative to the rest of the face, while a telephoto lens makes it look smaller.[1]

Portrait photography references note that very short lenses exaggerate the nose and shrink the ears, and that moderate telephoto lenses flatter faces through slight compression.[2] Camera position relative to the light also changes the result.[2]

A looksmax.org thread on photomaxxing asked members what cameras, lenses, tripods, lighting and editing they use.[3] One reply said the poster looked much better when standing back and using a DSLR with a natural-perspective lens than with a phone selfie camera.[3]

lore.intro: Community discussion frames photography as a way to control how a face is captured, with attention to lens, distance and lighting.[3]

claims.claim: Standing back with a real camera looks better than a close selfie.
claims.believers: One looksmax.org member said they look far better photographed from a distance with a DSLR than with a phone selfie camera.[3]
claims.experts: Photography references describe wide-angle lenses at close range as enlarging the nose and other nearby features, and longer lenses as flattening them.[1][2]

card.summary: Choosing angle, distance, lens and tilt to photograph well; the lens-distance physics is documented, attractiveness effects are untested.

quick.overview:
Photo angle maxxing means working out which camera angle, distance and head tilt produce the most flattering pictures of yourself.

Photography references document that close wide-angle shots enlarge nearby features and longer lenses flatten them. No studies test how such choices affect rated attractiveness.
quick.mechanism: Perspective depends mainly on camera-to-subject distance. Shooting from farther away with a longer focal length reduces the relative size difference between near and far facial features.
